issue_context.title: module meta function reset_connection does not populate {{ }} type variables when custom ansible_control_path is set
issue_context.body:
### Summary

The module meta's function: reset_connection, does not populate {{ }} type variables when custom ansible_control_path is set.

short:
executing:
`ansible -i inventory.yml testVM -m meta -a reset_connection -vvvv `

expected:
```
sending connection check: [b'ssh', b'-vvv', ..., b'ControlPath="/tmp/my_playbook-ssh-%h-testVM"', b'-O', b'check', b'172.30.20.81']
sending connection stop: [b'ssh', b'-vvv', ..., b'ControlPath="/tmp/my_playbook-ssh-%h-testVM"', b'-O', b'stop', b'172.30.20.81']
```

actual:
```
sending connection check: [b'ssh', b'-vvv', ..., b'ControlPath="/tmp/my_playbook-ssh-%h-{{ inventory_hostname }}"', b'-O', b'check', b'172.30.20.81']
No connection to reset: OpenSSH_8.9p1 Ubuntu-3, OpenSSL 3.0.2 15 Mar 2022`
Control socket connect(/tmp/my_playbook-ssh-172.30.20.81-{{ inventory_hostname }}): No such file or directory
```

Caused by {{ inverntory_hostname }} inside of ansible_control_path.
As suggested by @sivel  in related issue:
https://github.com/ansible/ansible/issues/76956#issuecomment-1031717511

### Issue Type

Bug Report

### Component Name

meta 
https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/plugins/connection/ssh.py

### Ansible Version

```console
$ ansible --version

  config file = /home/user/checkout/my_playbook/ansible.cfg
  configured module search path = ['/home/user/.ansible/plugins/modules', '/usr/share/ansible/plugins/modules']
  ansible python module location = /home/user/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/ansible
  ansible collection location = /home/user/.ansible/collections:/usr/share/ansible/collections
  executable location = /home/user/.local/bin/ansible
  python version = 3.10.6 (main, Nov 14 2022, 16:10:14) [GCC 11.3.0] (/usr/bin/python3)
  jinja version = 3.0.3
  libyaml = True
```


### Configuration

```console
$ ansible-config dump --only-changed -t all

==========

____________
ssh_args(/home/user/checkout/my_playbook/ansible.cfg) = -C -o ControlMaster=auto -o ControlPersist=1h

ssh:
___
ssh_args(/home/user/checkout/my_playbook/ansible.cfg) = -C -o ControlMaster=auto -o ControlPersist=1h
```


### OS / Environment

Ubuntu 22.04
Linux version 5.15.0-58-generic (buildd@lcy02-amd64-101) (gcc (Ubuntu 11.3.0-1ubuntu1~22.04) 11.3.0, GNU ld (GNU Binutils for Ubuntu) 2.38) #64-Ubuntu SMP Thu Jan 5 11:43:13 UTC 2023

### Steps to Reproduce

ansible.cfg:

```
[ssh_connection]
ssh_args = -C -o ControlMaster=auto -o ControlPersist=1h
```
Inventory.yml:
```
---
all:
  vars:
    ansible_control_path: "/tmp/my_playbook-ssh-%%h-{{ inventory_hostname }}"
    #ansible_control_path: "/tmp/my_playbook-ssh-%%h-testVM"  # <- using this line gives expected result
  hosts:
    testVM:
      ansible_host: "172.30.20.81"
```
1. Command to create ssh connection
```
ansible -i inventory.yml testVM -a "ping 9.9.9.9 -c 1"
```
2. Command to reset ssh connection
```
ansible -i inventory.yml testVM -m meta -a reset_connection -vvvv
```

My current workarround is using this task instead:
```
- name: reset ssh connection to allow user changes to affect 'current login user'
  shell: sleep 1; pkill -u {{ ansible_ssh_user }} sshd
  async: 5
  poll: 1
```

found here https://github.com/ansible/ansible/issues/66414#issuecomment-668517445

Thanks to @pakopent for the workaround!

Here to confirm that this also affects the `ansible_ssh_port` variable. My reproducer:
```yaml
# inventory.yml
---
all:
  hosts:
    testing:
      ansible_host: mysshhost.local

# playbook.yml
- hosts: all
  vars:
    some_dynamic_value: 22
    ansible_ssh_port: "{{ some_dynamic_value }}"
  tasks:
  - ansible.builtin.meta: reset_connection
```

Command to reproduce the error using the above files:
```
ansible-playbook playbook.yml --limit testing
```

The initial SSH connection works as expected, but the `reset_connection` meta call fails with the same output shown in this issue.

And version info:
```
ansible [core 2.15.3]
  config file = ansible.cfg
  configured module search path = ['~/.ansible/plugins/modules', '/usr/share/ansible/plugins/modules']

  libyaml = True
```

review_comments: Moving this to common code for consistency between the two paths makes sense, although I hope extra vars for connection plugins will be deprecated/phased out eventually, since now there's a way to document the variables, which also doubles as the argument spec and provides a consistent UX.
